Container.Name: mediawiki-plus
Container.Overview:
MediaWiki-Plus runs the official MediaWiki 1.43 LTS image extended with three extensions that are NOT bundled upstream:
* Variables - {{#var}} / {{#vardefine}} dynamic variables, needed by many template-heavy wikis. * PluggableAuth + OpenID Connect - optional single sign-on against any OIDC provider (Authelia, Keycloak, Authentik, Entra ID...). Both stay switched OFF unless you enable them.
Self-contained by default: the wiki stores its data in an integrated SQLite database inside the mapped "Database (SQLite)" folder, so no separate database container is required. An external MySQL/MariaDB server is supported too - see LocalSettings.example.php in the support repo.
The image is published at ghcr.io/jbowensii/mediawiki-plus and is pulled automatically. You do not need to build anything.
=== FIRST RUN: a one-time bootstrap is required === The official MediaWiki image has no environment-based database setup, so a brand new wiki has to be initialised once before it will serve pages. This is normal and takes about a minute. Full copy-and-paste walkthrough in the support README; the short version:
1) Fill in the Site Name, Site Server URL and Wiki Admin Password fields. Leave the "LocalSettings.php" path EMPTY. Click Apply. (Mounting LocalSettings.php before the file exists makes Docker create a DIRECTORY by that name, which breaks the wiki - that is why it starts blank.) 2) Open a console on the container and run maintenance/install.php once. This creates the SQLite schema and the admin account. 3) Copy LocalSettings.example.php from the support repo into your appdata folder as LocalSettings.php, point the container's "LocalSettings.php" field at it, and restart. 4) Run maintenance/update.php once to register the bundled and extra extensions.
=== REVERSE PROXY NOTE === This template defaults to bridge networking on host port 8080, which suits most setups. If your reverse proxy runs as an ipvlan container on a custom Docker network, it cannot reach published bridge ports on its own host - in that case switch Network to that custom network and give this container its own static IP instead.
Container.Requires: Nothing. The integrated SQLite database is used by default; an external MySQL/MariaDB server is optional.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Host port mapped to the container HTTP port (80). Put your reverse proxy in front of this.

Config.Name: Uploads (images)
Config.Description: Persistent storage for uploaded files and images.

Config.Name: Database (SQLite)
Config.Description: Integrated SQLite database directory (self-contained; holds the .sqlite file). Harmless to keep mapped even if you switch to MySQL/MariaDB.

Config.Name: Site Name
Config.Description: The name of your wiki, shown in the page title and the top-left of every page, e.g. My Project Wiki.

Config.Name: Site Server URL
Config.Description: Canonical URL of your wiki, e.g. https://wiki.example.com (no trailing slash). Use http://TOWER-IP:8080 if you are not using a reverse proxy.

Config.Name: DB Name
Config.Description: Database name. With SQLite the file will be this name plus .sqlite inside the Database folder.

Config.Name: Wiki Admin User
Config.Description: Local administrator username, created during the one-time bootstrap.

Config.Name: Wiki Admin Password
Config.Description: SET THIS. Password for the local administrator account. MediaWiki requires at least 10 characters.

Config.Name: LocalSettings.php (leave BLANK on first run)
Config.Description: Leave EMPTY for the very first start. After the one-time bootstrap, set this to your LocalSettings.php in appdata, e.g. /mnt/user/appdata/mediawiki-plus/LocalSettings.php

Config.Name: Secret Key
Config.Description: MediaWiki $wgSecretKey. Leave blank to let the bootstrap generate one, or paste a 64-character hex value to pin it.

Config.Name: Upgrade Key
Config.Description: MediaWiki $wgUpgradeKey. Leave blank to let the bootstrap generate one, or paste a 16-character value to pin it.

Config.Name: PHP upload max size
Config.Description: Optional PHP override (e.g. 64M) for larger uploads. Also raise $wgMaxUploadSize in LocalSettings.php.
